steps.title: What is Google Docs?
steps.body: Google Docs works like Word, but free in your browser. You need a Google account (for example a Gmail address). Go to docs.google.com and choose 'Blank document'.

steps.title: Typing and formatting
steps.body: Click on the white sheet and type. Want to make words bold or bigger? Select them with the mouse first, then click the B or the number at the top (for example 11) to change the size. Made a mistake? Press Backspace.

steps.title: Google saves for you
steps.body: You don't have to click 'Save' yourself: Google keeps your work automatically in your Google Drive. At the top is your document name; click it and type a clear name. Want it on paper? Choose File > Print.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a new document, type a short three-line letter, make the first line bold and give the document a name.

steps.title: What is Google Sheets?
steps.body: Google Sheets works like Excel: a big grid of boxes (cells) where you keep lists and calculate, for example your spending per month. Go to sheets.google.com and choose 'Blank'.

steps.title: Filling in numbers and text
steps.body: Click a box and type, for example 'Groceries' and in the box next to it '45'. Press Enter to go to the box below, or Tab to go to the right.

steps.title: Adding up numbers
steps.body: Put a column of numbers under each other. Click the box below, type =SUM(, select the numbers with the mouse and press Enter. Google adds everything up for you. Or click Σ at the top and choose 'SUM'.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a list of five expenses with an amount next to each and let Google Sheets calculate the total.

steps.title: What is Google Slides?
steps.body: Google Slides works like PowerPoint: a series of slides with text and photos, to show on a screen. Go to slides.google.com and choose 'Blank presentation'.

steps.title: Filling a slide
steps.body: The first slide has a title: click in it and type. For a new slide, click the plus at the top left. Keep the text short: a few words per line is enough.

steps.title: Adding a photo and presenting
steps.body: Choose Insert > Image > Upload from computer and drag the photo to the right spot. Click Present at the top right to show your slides full screen. Use the arrow keys to continue, and Esc to stop.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a three-slide presentation about your hobby, with at least one photo, and view it with 'Present'.
